name: disrespect
description: A judgment that a person, group, or thing has low value and is likely to produce a negative outcome. They are not worthy of your support and praise.
perceptions: This person, group, or thing has several important problems.
I'm not likely to trust their relevant actions in the future.

guidance.description: None of us can or should respect everything and everybody equally. A pure ban on disrespect is unworkable. We need a different approach to disrespect.
5 Ways to Stop the Cycle of Disrespect

variations.name: contempt
variations.description: A judgment that a person, group, or thing is socially or morally inferior and likely to produce a negative outcome. They are not worthy of your support and praise.
perceptions: This person or group is doing, saying, or represents something I disagree with.
This behavior or appearance indicates a lower social or moral status.

guidance.description: Contempt can be a valid response to certain behaviors. But we sometimess contempt more broadly than necessary. If you'd like to explore the root of contemptuous feelings, here are some articles to consider.
If you perceive that someone is being contemptuous towards you, this article may be of interest.

examples: Assuming someone is untrustworthy because they hold a certain political opinion.

variations.name: bullying contempt
variations.description: A feeling of dislike-for and superiority-over someone mainly to raise your status or distract attention about your behavior.
perceptions: That person is being treated well.
I need to let others know why they're lower status than me.

guidance.description: If you started noticing that you are tearing people apart with criticism, frequently point out their minor faults and ridicule them for any mistakes they make, make fun of their flaws it might be a good time to stop and reflect on your actions and their effect of your life and the lives of others.

variations.name: contempt for the childish
variations.description: A feeling of dislike-for and superiority-over someone due to a judgment that their behavior is silly or not age-appropriate for the context.
perceptions: That person is not taking this situation serious enough.

guidance.description: Whether we like it or not, we will all eventually meet, perhaps in a work or volunteer situation, an impossibly immature person.

commentaries.quote: We accuse others of what we cannot accept in ourselves.
You cannot disrespect the caterpillar, while raving about the butterfly.
Contempt is a way to signal to someone that we're higher status than them in some characteristic. And it's a way to communicate to everyone listening which characteristics we value.
The experience of contempt is powered by adrenaline, which makes us feel temporarily more confident and self-righteous but at the same time, less humane.

Admit it. It’s fun to feel like others are beneath us. There are only two ways to feel superior: Elevate yourself or demote others. Sneering down is uplifting, especially when we’ve hit a ceiling and can’t elevate ourselves higher. If you can’t get to the top, dissing others is the only other way to feel like you have. Besides, sometimes we’re right. Plenty of people deserve to be taken down a peg, though of course that could include us when we’re sneering.
Preservation of one's own culture does not require contempt or disrespect for other cultures.
